hints: Start with the given $300 \text{ Hz}$ and $600 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the wavelength using $v = f\lambda$.
Compare the $0.50 \text{ m}$ separation with that wavelength to find what fraction of a full wave fits between the points.
Recall that one full wavelength corresponds to $360^\circ$ of phase, so multiply the fraction by $360^\circ$.
walkthrough: Note the given data: frequency $f = 300 \text{ Hz}$, speed $v = 600 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and separation $x = 0.50 \text{ m}$.
Use the wave equation $v = f\lambda$ to find the wavelength: $\lambda = v / f$.
Substitute with units: $\lambda = 600 \text{ m s}^{-1} / 300 \text{ Hz} = 2.0 \text{ m}$.
Find the fraction of a wavelength in the separation: $x / \lambda = 0.50 \text{ m} / 2.0 \text{ m} = 0.25$.
Convert fraction of a wave to phase difference using $360^\circ$ per wavelength: phase difference $= 0.25 \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ$.

options.A: 45 degrees would correspond to only $0.25 \text{ m}$, which is one-eighth of the $2.0 \text{ m}$ wavelength, not the $0.50 \text{ m}$ separation.
options.B: A $0.50 \text{ m}$ separation is one-quarter of the $2.0 \text{ m}$ wavelength, giving one-quarter of $360^\circ$, which is $90^\circ$.
options.C: 180 degrees needs half a wavelength separation, which would be $1.0 \text{ m}$ here, twice the given $0.50 \text{ m}$.
options.D: 360 degrees needs a full wavelength separation of $2.0 \text{ m}$, not $0.50 \text{ m}$.
